Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

even if conjunction

also even supposing, granted that

classical

Cic. Amic. 104: omnia autem brevia tolerābilia esse dēbent, etiamsī magna sunt

etiamsī (etiam sī)

conjunction, with the moods of sī: indicative for a real case, subjunctive for a supposed one

The main clause often has tamen. Plain et sī or sī … tamen says the same.

Other words

  • etsī — even if

    conjunction, with the moods of sī · also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. etsi

    The same word as etiamsī, but in classical prose mostly of a fact, “although” (see that record).

  • ut (+ subjunctive) — granted that, even supposing

    conjunction, with the subjunctive · also used · classical · Ov. Pont. 3.4.79: ut dēsint vīrēs, tamen est laudanda voluntās (Lewis & Short)

    Concessive ut: “suppose that”, answered by tamen.

  • quamvīs (+ subjunctive) — even if, however much

    conjunction, with the subjunctive · also used · classical · Ov. Rem. 213–214: tū tantum quamvīs firmīs retinēbere vinclīs, ī procul

    See although.

Examples

  • omnia autem brevia tolerābilia esse dēbent, etiamsī magna sunt

    and everything short ought to be bearable, even if it is greatCic. Amic. 104

  • quīcumque turpī fraude semel innōtuit, etiam sī vērum dīcit, āmittit fidem

    whoever has once been known for a shameful lie loses trust even if he tells the truthPhaedr. 1.10.1–2

  • nūllus sūmptus est, et sī sūmptus esset, tamen valētūdinis causā experīrēs

    it costs nothing, and even if it did cost something, you would still try it for your healthCato Agr. 157

  • ut dēsint vīrēs, tamen est laudanda voluntās

    even if the strength is lacking, the will deserves praiseOv. Pont. 3.4.79 (Lewis & Short)

  • tū tantum quamvīs firmīs retinēbere vinclīs, ī procul, et longās carpere perge viās

    only, even if strong ties hold you back, go far away, and set out on long roadsOv. Rem. 213–214

See also although, if.
